messages:
jena: Starting onboarding for the new 'orchid' region (us-west-4) — goal: provision an EKS GPU cluster for production inference. We'll use Pulumi for cluster & nodepool resources and Terraform for network/IAM/peering. Primary deliverable: CI + remote state wiring and handoff to Platform SRE once green.

omar: +1. Couple of immediate items: request EC2 quota for p4d, check ENI limits per AZ, and confirm the CIDR doesn't overlap with existing peered regions.

samira: Sounds good. For GPUs: are we standardizing on p4d.24xlarge for latency-sensitive pools or do we want a mixed approach?

jena: Plan is p4d for latency-critical inference (initial commit) and g5 for cheaper batch workloads. We'll set autoscaling groups and nodegroup taints/tolerations. Cost ballpark: p4d ~ $30-35/hr, g5 ~ $5-8/hr (region dependent). We'll add cost alerts.

kai: For state backend: Terraform -> S3 + DynamoDB (locking). Pulumi -> S3 backend (self-hosted). I'll provision two buckets: redwood-tf-state-orchid and redwood-pulumi-orchid with SSE-KMS, and a DynamoDB table tf-state-locks-orchid. Commands for local dev/CI:
```bash
# terraform
terraform init -backend-config="bucket=redwood-tf-state-orchid" -backend-config="key=orchid/network.tfstate" -backend-config="dynamodb_table=tf-state-locks-orchid"

# pulumi
pulumi login s3://redwood-pulumi-orchid
pulumi stack init orchid/prod
```

lex: CI plan: GH Actions workflow 'orchid-provision.yml' with steps: tf fmt/validate, terraform plan (comment), pulumi preview, and gated apply requiring two approvers. CI role uses least privilege keys scoped to the buckets + DynamoDB + assume-role for apply. We should avoid giving CI full EC2 perms.

infra-bot: Ticket created: INFR-894 — S3 buckets + DynamoDB table provisioning for orchid region.

omar: I'll draft the IAM role policy; suggest splitting into: network-admin (vpc/route/peering), cluster-admin (eks, nodegroups), state-admin (s3/dynamodb). CI will assume state-admin for plan and assume cluster-admin only with manual approval.

samira: Cluster bootstrap checklist I want automated in Pulumi: driver daemonset, nvidia device plugin, kube-proxy config, aws-vpc-cni settings for ENI scaling. Example GPU daemonset manifest we will apply as part of boot: 
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: nvidia-driver-installer
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      tolerations:
      - key: "nvidia.com/gpu"
        operator: Exists
      containers:
      - name: installer
        image: "nvidia/driver-installer:latest"
        securityContext:
          privileged: true
```

kai: Validation automation (to run from CI after apply):
- terraform plan returns no changes
- pulumi preview returns no changes
- kubectl get nodes -> all nodes Ready + label "nvidia.com/gpu.present=true"
- run small inference job (docker image: redwood/orchid-smoke) against local LB, target p50 < 150ms
- verify metrics: GPU utilization > 5% and < 95% during smoke; alert if OOMs or driver errors in logs
- run cost smoke: query billing api for projected daily spend and ensure within threshold

lex: Networking checks: VPC peering status, route table propagation, NAT gateway count, security group egress rules for model download endpoints, and verify no 0.0.0.0/0 open rules on control plane ports. Also confirm shared services (observability, s3 endpoints) are reachable.

jena: Handoff checklist to Platform SRE (must be in the final runbook):
- ARNs for S3 buckets and DynamoDB lock table + list of IAM roles and trust policies
- GH Actions workflow links + required approvers
- Links to Pulumi/Terraform module repos and branch used for the run
- Dashboards: cluster health, GPU temperature, GPU memory by pod, node termination/spot eviction rates
- Runbook: how to drain GPU nodes gracefully, roll back to smaller model variant, and steps to reprovision nodegroups if drivers fail
- Canary plan: 1% traffic for 2h with rollback if error rate > 1% or p95 latency > 500ms

kai: I'll open PRs for the Pulumi cluster module and Terraform network module today and attach the sample policies. Omar — can you review the IAM policy when it's up? Lex — can you add the GH Actions gating?

omar: Will review this afternoon. Also created request with cloud quotas team for p4d quota bump to 10 instances in the account (case #Q-17233). Keep me posted if we need more.

deploy-bot: GitHub: Created workflow 'orchid-ci' in repo infra/playbooks — reviewers required: @omar, @lex.

jena: Thanks everyone. I'll schedule the first full run tomorrow 06:00 UTC; I expect the CI will run create->validate->smoke. If green, we'll move to handoff. I'll post the runbook draft to the docs folder after the first run.
